meta.name: Agent Skills Security Self-assessment (Retro-OS Skin)
meta.description: Windows 95 system skin for a two-language security self-assessment: the app reads as one program window (os-window + taskbar + system dialogs) standing on the teal desktop, drawn from the classic bevel triad and the classic 16-colour system palette.

color.palette_type: system (classic Win95 triad on a teal desktop; white document fields)

primary.role: Title bars, selection highlight, primary accent, info state

secondary.role: Medium shadow grey — borders, tracks, disabled title-bar glyphs

accent.role: Alters nothing: navy replaces the removed editorial orange; chrome text text-status uses the same navy as selection

neutral.usage: The classic bevel triad: highlight #FFFFFF, face #C0C0C0, light shadow #DFDFDF, dark shadow #808080, outer border #000000; #404040 micro-labels (7.5:1 on the chrome face)

semantic.role_split: One meaning, two roles: headline TEXT uses --color-score-green/amber/red, bar/graphic FILL uses --color-success/warning/error — both sets are the same dark classic hexes. Worst-case black-on-white floors documented in the token layer: #008000 4.75:1, #808000 3.55:1 (large text / fill only), #800000 7.5:1

graphics_only.usage: Bright system tints declared graphics-only (1–2:1 on white; never carry text). #FF0000 is also the flat red of the warn dialog circle

color.contrast_strategy: Dark members of the classic 16-colour set for all text on white/face fields; every ratio measured and documented in css/theme-retro-os.css token comments

headline.font: W95FA via --font-heading, except the Welcome Splash catchphrase which runs Silkscreen 32px (uppercase, 36px on the Chinese page)
headline.letter_spacing: normal (pixel faces carry their own rhythm)

font_families.heading: W95FA (Latin chrome) / Fusion Pixel 12 SC subset (Han chrome on the Chinese page, leading --font-heading under html[lang^="zh"]), fallback Segoe UI/SimSun
font_families.display: Silkscreen — the Welcome Splash catchphrase only, Latin-pinned

typography.font_style_notes: All three faces are self-hosted under fonts/ with their OFL 1.1 texts and fonts/PROVENANCE.md — W95FA (Alina Sava, pixel re-creation of MS Sans Serif), Silkscreen (Jason Kottke, bitmap display face), Fusion Pixel 12px proportional SC (TakWolf) as an offline repo-side subset of the pinned release. Each is pinned by unicode-range so Latin and Han runs never land on the other's face; no third-party network dependency (ADR 0001, ADR 0021 amended by #51). UI chrome only; prose stays on the readable body stack.

spacing.content_density: the window frame owns the whitespace: #app padding varies per breakpoint (64/48/24 top)
spacing.section_rhythm: consistent rhythm off --space-2..--space-5 inside dialog bodies (8/16/32px)

layout.grid_system: single column; the application container reads as ONE program window standing on the desktop (.os-window wraps #app: the frame's opaque chrome face reserves the bevel as its edge, the client area sits inside it)

chrome_dimensions.taskbar: 36px fixed at viewport bottom, height reserved on body

breakpoints.mobile: max-width 480px (dialog anatomy stacks, Start menu spans)

layout.alignment_tendency: left-aligned content on centered windows; dialog buttons right-aligned

border_radius.exception: 32px circle only for the drawn dialog icons

shape.border_usage: none — depth is drawn with box-shadow bevels, not borders
shape.divider_style: 1px solid #000000 rule under an open expander's title-bar row

elevation.shadow_style: no drop shadows — the bevel triad IS the elevation

levels.low: --bevel-sunken: inset -1px -1px #FFFFFF, inset 1px 1px #000000, inset -2px -2px #DFDFDF, inset 2px 2px #808080 (fields, tracks, pressed buttons)
levels.medium: --bevel-raised: inset -1px -1px #000000, inset 1px 1px #FFFFFF, inset -2px -2px #808080, inset 2px 2px #DFDFDF (buttons, window frames, dialog faces)
levels.high: desktop z-ladder: .os-shortcuts 100 (the icon column on the desktop's BASE surface — icons are surface, not chrome) < .os-window 200 (the Window stack's rung: every Window paints WINDOW_Z_BASE + its stack number, so a Window always covers the column) < taskbar 1000 < start menu 1100 < about/dialog 1200, over dims rgba(0,0,0,0.25)

elevation.depth_cues: flat layering: background never eases; pressed state flips raised → sunken; taskbar state flips program button sunken/raised

iconography.style: flat circles and system flag marks, all CSS-drawn — no icon font, no image assets
iconography.stroke_weight: solid fills (4px cross bars, 2px wireframe ink)
iconography.size_scale: 32px dialog icons, 16×14 title-bar buttons, 16×14 start flag
iconography.preferred_set: hand-drawn era set: red circle + white cross (warn), navy circle (info), [—][□][×] title marks, [+] / [-] Explorer toggles, etched radio dial glyph, four-colour flag gradient

motion.easing: none — Win95 has no easing; every token transition is 0s and all value animations use steps()
motion.mechanical_traces: os-wireframe-trace 200ms: a navy rectangle sweeps from the title bar downward in four steps(4) across the first 160ms, content pops in behind it in one step at the 100ms midpoint (os-view-pop), and the ink lifts off in a fifth step over the final 40ms — restarts every time a view re-enters rendering via App.showView
motion.entrance_pattern: card wipe (client-area) on question change; view pop behind the trace
motion.boot: sessionStorage-gated splash (flag 'quiz-os-booted'); masked overlay + segmented stepped fill synced to SPLASH_MS 1350 in js/boot.js, 200ms linear fade handoff; the gate shows exactly ONE trace, never splash+fade double
motion.reduced_motion_contract: prefers-reduced-motion: no trace draws, no gated content — full content present immediately; blocks gate disjoint selectors in css/theme-retro-os.css and css/quiz.css (card wipes, Progress Fill, Blind-Spot Bar width easing); boot.js decides to skip the splash outright

components: os-window (raised frame on the teal desktop: the frame paints an opaque chrome face and its padding reserves the bevel, #app fills the client area inside that edge — tickets #60/#71; on the results and review views it is positioned by the window's Geometry and carries a corner size grip)

title bar (navy→#1084D0 gradient, 14px W95FA label, [—][□][×] controls drawn as inline-SVG era glyphs — 6×2 bar, 9×9 square, 8×7 cross in currentColor, black live / gray disabled, #49; the ONE window chrome — the results header no longer fakes a window of its own)
taskbar (start button + program button + the two-segment EN/中文 Language Toggle that replaced the clock tray, #50; pressed-state flip on minimize)
start menu popup and about/system dialog primitive (js/windows.js App.Windows.openSystemDialog: backdrop dims desktop 25%, one dialog at a time, closes only by button/Escape)
boot splash (sunken groove, segmented navy stepped fill, status line)

welcome splash (the compact landing wizard card, #53: 64px inline eye glyph, two-line uppercase catchphrase on the Silkscreen display face — 32px, the Fusion Pixel subset carrying it on the Chinese page at 36px — the Bank's title as subtitle, a hairline rule, one body line + time estimate, a single default [Start] — the language affordance is the taskbar toggle, never a dialog)

locale-swap failure notice (`.quiz-notice` inside the current view: raised bevel strip, localized copy naming the other language, a beveled dismiss button, auto-dismissed; the language never changes unless the swap succeeds, #55/#56)

quiz status bar (pinned inside the fixed-height window, quiz view only, 32px: segmented navy Progress Fill on a 150×14 track + question counter + phase name; segmented = repeating gradient trick; only .quiz-body scrolls)

question card / wizard (a flat grouping element since #52 — the raised card frame is gone; the sunken scenario field and the radiogroup rows with etched dial glyphs carry the depth; pinned footer [< Back] [Next >] / [Finish])
title card (results window: navy bar + sunken white client field, percentage in --color-score-*)
risk radar (sunken white field, black-on-white vector chart)
blind-spot bars (sunken dithered track — 1px repeating-conic dither, graphics-only; square dark fills)

action plan + expanders (action plan = ONE ranked list: the Actions are rows in a single sunken white field — sunken priority badge, title, AST chip, description, hairline separators, no navy head row and no raised card frame, #72; the Narrative Expander and the Review accordion share the Explorer disclosure idiom — a silver row led by the square [+]/[-] glyph, black on the face, never navy; the Deep-Dive Prompt keeps no expander at all, #74 — its window body is the one-line guidance above a sunken scrolling prompt field, and its single Copy Prompt command sits in the window's flat bar, the same strip surface as the Quiz menu bar with no menu in it)
command buttons on every surface (raised bevel, dotted focus rectangle, sunken press)

aesthetic.visual_metaphor: an operating system desktop from 1995 — the assessment is a program, participants are system users
aesthetic.era_influence: Windows 95 (classic bevel triad, 16-colour system palette, MS Sans Serif chrome)
aesthetic.genre: productivity software parody carrying a serious assessment

visual_language.ornamentation: none that is not structural: dithering only on graphics-only fills, bevels only where a control sits
visual_language.whitespace_usage: measured — the window frame defines space; dialog interiors are tight (8/16px)
visual_language.visual_weight_distribution: chrome-dense frames around quiet white content fields
visual_language.focal_strategy: title bars and stepped navy fills carry all visual weight
visual_language.contrast_level: high (black on white inside windows; navy-on-white chrome)

composition.hierarchy_method: window nesting: dialog → panel → field; inside windows the largest text is the percentage headline
composition.flow_direction: top-down inside one window (wizard); the taskbar anchors the bottom
composition.grouping_strategy: sunken panels group; expanded tree children indent
composition.negative_space_role: teal desktop margin frames the program

imagery.graphic_elements: CSS-drawn era icons and logo marks

interaction_feel.feedback_style: instant facet-flips: raised→sunken, selection → navy block with white text
interaction_feel.hover_behavior: same raised state; focus dot rectangle only
interaction_feel.microinteraction_density: low — flips, no easing, no ripples

brand_voice_in_ui.tone: period-system voice: terse status lines ('Not a test — a mirror.'),
brand_voice_in_ui.empty_state_approach: sunken field with a one-line status
brand_voice_in_ui.error_tone: era error dialog: red circle, frank statement, one action

overview.performance_tier: high (no images, no easing libraries, self-hosted fonts)
overview.fallback_strategy: box-shadow bevels degrade to flat bounds; motion is fully optional under prefers-reduced-motion
overview.primary_technology: pure CSS (gradients, clip-path, steps()); zero animation JS

background_effects.description: #008080 desktop at body level; window faces flat

trigger_points: view enters the window (App.showView un-hides a section)
client-area card swap in the wizard
scroll_triggered_animations.animation_type: stepped wireframe trace + one-step content pop / card wipe

text_effects.description: pixel face carries its own rendering; text-shadow only on disabled chrome glyphs

glassmorphism_neumorphism.style: the opposite of glass: opaque bevels

visual_effects.composite_notes: Everything is drawn with box-shadow bevels, gradient steps and a two-circle pseudo-element icon system. Motion budget is spent once per view entry (the 200ms trace) and inside the wizard (wipes); everywhere else answers are instant, and the reduced-motion contract removes even those.
